title: XIV. Effect of the union: communion of natures and communication of idioms; Cap.2 close toward Cap.3
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER THREE follows, On ye offices belonging toward Jesus Christ. — And because ye idioms belonging toward both natures stand as attributed indifferently to ye person signified by concrete words, therefore on account belonging toward ye difference belonging toward natures it stands as sometimes usual to add according to which nature ye predicate belongs to ye subject. — For just as ye unity belonging toward person and ye personal union, so also ye distinction belonging toward ye two natures in Christ stands as necessarily retained. — Damascene calls this an exchange belonging toward names, and Melanchthon defines ye predication in which a property belonging to one nature stands as attributed to ye person in ye concrete. — but through concretes one stands as rightly declared belonging toward ye other, and ye property and operation belonging toward ye one belonging toward ye other — as God stands as human, ye human stands as God, God suffered and died, ye human stands as eternal and made heaven and earth. — Therefore it stands as unlawful to say absolutely that God suffered, or that a human created heaven; — For ye reason why one nature stands as predicated belonging toward ye other stands as none other than ye hypostatic union in ye same supposit. — On account belonging toward it they stand as predicated belonging toward one another — not absolutely and abstractly, but through concrete words that involve ye supposit and connote ye personality in which ye natures agree. — The effect belonging toward ye personal union stands as ye communion both belonging toward ye natures and belonging toward ye properties, which stands as called ye communication belonging toward idioms. — XIV.
pass_b_english: XIV. The effect of the personal union is the communion both of the natures and of the properties, which is called the communication of idioms. On account of it they are predicated of one another — not absolutely and abstractly, but through concrete words that involve the supposit and connote the personality in which the natures agree. For the reason why one nature is predicated of the other is none other than the hypostatic union in the same supposit.

Therefore it is unlawful to say absolutely that God suffered, or that a human created heaven; but through concretes one is rightly declared of the other, and the property and operation of the one of the other — as God is human, the human is God, God suffered and died, the human is eternal and made heaven and earth. Damascene calls this an exchange of names, and Melanchthon defines the predication in which a property belonging to one nature is attributed to the person in the concrete. For just as the unity of person and the personal union, so also the distinction of the two natures in Christ is necessarily retained. And because the idioms of both natures are attributed indifferently to the person signified by concrete words, therefore on account of the difference of natures it is sometimes usual to add according to which nature the predicate belongs to the subject.
CHAPTER THREE follows, On the offices of Jesus Christ.
source_text: XIV. Effectus unionis personalis est communio tum naturarum, tum proprietatum, quae dicitur communicatio idiomatum. Propter quam de se invicem praedicantur, non quidem absolute & abstracte, sed per vocabula concreta quae involvunt suppositum, & connotant personalitatem, in qua naturae conveniunt. Nam ratio, propter quam una natura de altera praedicatur, nulla est alia, quam unio hypostatica in eodem supposito. Quapropter nefas est dicere absolute Deum esse passum, aut hominem creasse caelum; sed per concreta recte unum de altero, & proprietas atque operatio alterius de altero enunciabitur, ut Deus est homo, homo est Deus, Deus est passus & mortuus, homo est aeternus, condidit caelum & terram. Damascenus appellat antidosis onomaton, & Melanchthon finit praedicationem, in qua proprietas uni naturae conveniens tribuitur personae in concreto. Ut enim unitas personae & unio personalis, ita & duarum naturarum in Christo distinctio necessario retinetur. Quia vero personae per vocabula concreta significatae utriusque naturae idiomata indifferenter tribuuntur, idcirco propter discrimen naturarum, ut sciatur secundum utram naturam praedicatum subiecto conveniat, addi id ipsum nonnunquam solet. CAPUT TERTIUM sequitur, De officiis Iesu Christi.
